transcript.text: Samsung RS68A8820S9/EU flashing 22E on the display and the fridge side isn't as cold as it should be. What does 22E mean and can I fix it?

On Samsung models like yours, code 22E typically indicates an issue with the evaporator fan in the freezer section. This fan pushes cold air into the fridge; if it stops working due to ice jamming the blades or a motor failure, the fridge side will warm up while the freezer stays cold. To help narrow this down: when the appliance is running, do you hear any faint humming or whirring from inside the freezer compartment (usually behind the back panel), or is it completely silent? Also, please check if there is any visible ice buildup on the food items in the fridge section or frost accumulating heavily at the back of the freezer.

There's an occasional ticking/scraping sound from inside the fridge back panel, not really a hum. There's a bit of frost around the vent at the top back of the fridge, and airflow from the fridge vents is very weak. No burning smell or tripping, by the way.

The ticking or scraping sound you hear is very likely the evaporator fan blades hitting ice or debris, which suggests why airflow is weak and the fridge side isn't cooling properly. Before we consider replacing parts, let's check if a blocked drain is causing the ice to form in the first place. Please look at the bottom of the back wall inside the fridge compartment for a small drain hole; is it clear and dry, or is there water/ice blocking it?
I'm not sure where the drain hole is, and I can't tell from looking. I can't remove the inner back panel and won't try. Is there anything else I can check from the front?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. The 22E code on your Samsung suggests a fault with the evaporator fan, which is why you hear that scraping sound as ice hits the blades. Since you cannot remove panels to check the drain or clear the ice manually right now, let's rule out simple blockages first. Please check if the vents inside the fridge (usually at the top back) are blocked by food items or containers. If they are clear but it still isn't cooling well after 24 hours, the ice is likely blocking the fan behind the panel, which will require a full manual defrost (unplugging for 24 hours) to temporarily fix.

The vents at the top back of the fridge aren't blocked by food, they're clear. Do I really need to unplug it for 24 hours? I've got lots of food to keep cold, though I do have a cool box. Is there anything else I should check first?

You don't need to unplug it for 24 hours if you have your cool box ready; that method is only for when you can't move the food. Since the vents are clear but airflow is weak and there's frost at the back, this points strongly to a defrost system fault (like a failed heater or thermostat) rather than just a blocked drain. The '22E' code suggests the fan is struggling against ice. To confirm this without opening panels: does your model have a 'No Frost' label inside? If so, listen at night for a faint hiss or bubbling from the freezer back (the defrost cycle running). Also, is the compressor running continuously without cycling off?

I'm not sure whether there's a 'No Frost' label, I haven't seen one. I haven't listened at night for a hiss or bubbling, and I can't tell if the compressor is cycling. Is there anything else I can check from the front, or should I get it looked at?

Given the flashing 22E code, weak airflow, and visible frost at the back of the fridge compartment, this is probably a fault with the automatic defrost system (likely the heater, thermostat or sensor) rather than just a simple blockage. Because you cannot remove the internal panels to clear the ice manually without risking damage to seals or wiring, and because the underlying component has failed, this requires an engineer to diagnose and replace the part safely. In the meantime, keep your cool box ready for emergencies and try to minimise how often you open the doors to preserve what cold remains.

Ice buildup blocking the fan or air vents (medium)
